principles: Project lower-layer truth; do not replace lifecycle, proof, freshness, DONE, or Authority semantics.
Fail honest: unavailable lower-layer capabilities render unknown or unavailable, never green.
Implement only correctness gaps named by the execution plan; avoid arbitrary optimization or broad cleanup.
Separate story-level gate blockers from project-level queue health in every output.
Guard every mutating queue exception write with audit metadata and write coordination.
drivers: High-risk lifecycle/state-machine surface: wrong output can cause false DONE or false cleanup.
The user requested the whole plan completed, so Appendix D admissibility_waterline and expanded queue exception details are in scope.
Operators need a concrete CLI surface that replaces manual stitching across session_brief, story_authority_resolve, lifecycle_check, and proof diagnostics.

options.name: A: Minimal command wrapper over existing status commands
cons: Does not satisfy Appendix D waterline, queue exception registry, expanded batch view, CP-0/CP-4 unified view, or product-visible completion criterion
Still leaves hosts stitching multiple outputs manually

options.name: B: Implement read-only projectors, Appendix D waterline, and guarded queue exception write
pros: Matches the execution plan end to end without creating a second lifecycle/proof system
Gives operators one mechanical status surface and durable experiment grouping
Implements the required waterline entry point as diagnostic-only rather than faking proof completion
cons: Touches command registration, process facts, lifecycle-control core, proof-admissibility projection, and tests
Requires careful compatibility updates to existing structural smoke

options.name: C: Full new lifecycle-control enforcement engine
pros: Could centralize all lifecycle control in one subsystem
cons: Violates the plan by replacing existing lifecycle/proof/DONE ownership
High risk of inconsistent logic and false authority over lower-layer gates

chosen: B: Implement read-only projectors, Appendix D waterline, and guarded queue exception write
rationale: Option B is the only choice that satisfies the user request to complete the whole plan while preserving host-neutral layering. It implements the missing control-plane commands, includes Appendix D waterline as a diagnostic projection, and limits mutation to the explicitly guarded queue exception path.

preMortem.scenario: Control plane accidentally becomes a second lifecycle gate
preMortem.trigger: Projector recomputes phase readiness or proof eligibility instead of consuming lower-layer results
preMortem.consequence: Hosts may trust inconsistent status and advance or block incorrectly
preMortem.mitigation: Only consume resolveStoryAuthority, StoryReadinessReport, Proof Admissibility diagnostics/waterline rows, and explicit queue registry data; tests assert no lifecycle/evidence mutation from status commands.

preMortem.trigger: Waterline status is treated as an independent source of truth instead of a derived diagnostic projection
preMortem.consequence: Candidate or diagnostic evidence could appear to satisfy DONE
preMortem.mitigation: Waterline output states diagnosticOnly=true; tests assert candidate/diagnostic/legacy cannot satisfy DONE through either waterline or control-plane projection.

preMortem.scenario: Tier-C experiment stories get cleaned as duplicates
preMortem.trigger: Duplicate classifier runs before experiment exception precedence or exception registry is malformed
preMortem.consequence: Experiment evidence is destroyed or hidden
preMortem.mitigation: Implement precedence cleanup-required > active-worktree > experiment-batch-exception > duplicate-candidate, expanded view, and malformed cleanup-required visibility.

preMortem.trigger: Handler writes process events, evidence, story metadata, or git artifacts while building status
preMortem.consequence: Status checks change the state they are supposed to observe
preMortem.mitigation: Snapshot story files/process-events/git status in smoke tests around global_control_status, runtime_closure_status, queue_governance_status, and admissibility_waterline.

preMortem.trigger: queue_exception_set writes shared registry without main lock or audit binding
preMortem.consequence: Concurrent hosts can race and produce unreviewable exception state
preMortem.mitigation: Use main write lock for shared registry writes and persist policyVersion/class/membership/source/storyFilesHash/dashboardMode/cleanupPolicy/actor/reason/timestamp.
